core.store.note: macOS uses the data-protection keychain where entitled; an unentitled process (an unsigned CLI) keeps the file-based keychain and storeStatus() reports legacy-keychain.

core.copy.note: ErrorCopy serves the generated Copy.generated.swift tables: message(code)/title(code) look a code up in COPY_CODES, then COPY_GATE, then COPY_ACTIVATION; activationMessage/activationTitle (and ActivationResult.message/title) read COPY_ACTIVATION only; an unknown code reads COPY_FALLBACK naming it; {name} placeholders are filled from params or dropped; setOverrides is the host's English layer. The hand-written table is gone; PolarisCopy's gate titles and subtitles default to the gate table (ErrorCopyTests).

core.backend.note: client.backend (PolarisKey.BackendClient): data(for:) and headers() send X-PKey-License and X-PKey-Device only; backendOrigins (exact scheme/host/port, https except loopback) is checked before the request and on every redirect hop before it is sent; the freshness pre-sync, one shared sync, one forced sync and retry on license_stale/license_invalid (at least 10 s apart), and not_entitled/sign_in_required thrown typed. BackendTests replays backend-matrix.json's client rows.

license.manage.note: PX-W8: the device-limit result exposes manageUrl (validated), plus the return and key helpers.

config.resolve.note: Member names compare by scalar value, but JSONValue keeps the first of two canonically equivalent names (WIRE-CONTRACT-V3 §10).

config.mirror.note: The Swift mirror is rendered by tools/gen-mirrors.ts.

config.local.note: config.set, clear and clearAll persist through a LocalConfigStore (UserDefaults by default), validate against the catalog and raise client.events .config; config.setting(key) returns a handle whose current() gives the effective value, its source and lock, and onConfigChange(key | "*", listener) returns a cancellable ConfigSubscription (configChanges(key) is the AsyncStream form), fed by the same change observation as client.events for local writes and syncs (LocalConfigTests).

devices.attest.note: client.devices.attest() (PolarisKey/DevicesClient.swift): POST devices/attest/challenge, DCAppAttestService.attestKey over SHA-256(UTF-8(requestHash)) through PolarisKeyPlatform's AppAttestClient, POST devices/attest; the key id kept in the Keychain (account app_attest_key) and re-attested with a fresh key when a reinstall, migration or restore killed it. Registered as Core's attestor so a 403 attestation_required edge-mint or commerce claim attests once and retries once. Unsupported runtime on macOS and where App Attest does not run (the simulator); outlet on an iOS build with an embedded provisioning profile.

identity.oidc.note: Native browser sign-in (loopback, scheme, claimed HTTPS) waits on I-15; the host-supplied https redirect is identity.redirect.web. The device-code route is client.identity.signIn.start(SignInOptions(browser:)), which opens the device-code verification URL in ASWebAuthenticationSession; session.wait() polls /identity/auth/device/poll (identity.devicecode; the old /identity/auth/poll is retired and the Worker no longer serves it).

identity.devicelabel.note: PX-W13: normalizeDeviceLabel over Unicode scalars, CoreOptions.deviceName and the platform default (macOS Host.current().localizedName, iOS-family UIDevice.current.name), on signIn.start, activation and registration; SignInPrompt.deviceName is the Worker's echo. PolarisKeyUI has no device-code sign-in view to show it in (ui.kit is planned and unowned).

identity.redirect.web.note: signIn.start(SignInOptions(channel: .redirect, redirectUri:)) builds the S256 authorize URL from discovery (IdentityRedirect, CryptoKit) for a browser the host opens; session.complete(callbackUrl:) checks the redirect URI, state and iss before anything is sent, then redeems the code at discovery's token endpoint. Single use; a refusal is a typed SignInError and never wipes the token. Loopback, scheme and claimed-HTTPS redirects are I-15's; the licence choice (license_choice=app) is identity.choice.

identity.choice.note: SignInOptions(licenseChoice: .app) sends license_choice=app (only when discovery lists the four choice routes; else the card chooses) and session.complete(callbackUrl:) then settles .chooseLicense(PendingSignIn); identity.choice.licenses/devices/complete/cancel(grant:) take the grant, store the device token on complete like a sign-in, and throw a typed ChoiceError (invalid_grant, license_choice_required and device_limit with a fresh view, not_found, rate_limited with retryAfterSeconds); UnsupportedError(product) when a route is not published. LicenseChoiceModel (PolarisKeyUICore, @Observable) drives the LicenseChoice screen's KitInputs from the SDK.

identity.exchange.note: identity.exchange(kind:subjectToken:nonce:) and exchangeNonce(kind:) (PolarisKeyIdentity): the nonce route registers the device keys, the token route takes the pkey-proof/1 exchange proof over nonce.key and the token hash; the outcome is signedIn, confirm (PendingConsent, completed through identity.choice.complete(grant:choice:consent:)), choose, needsSignIn or unavailable, and refusals are a typed ExchangeError. A 404 on either route, a discovery with no exchange member or a memory-only key port is unavailable with no request. Replayed against the exchange-* transcripts (TranscriptTests). Sign in with Apple itself is I-44.4.

identity.autosignin.note: autoSignIn() rungs 1-4 (plan-auto-sign-in §1, I-44): a stored sign-in, then the platform provider's silent mode where it has one (Apple has none; Game Center is I-44.5), then its one sheet under prompt: .optional; every refusal is a result.

release.fetch.note: client.update.fetch(version:buildId:size:sha256:to:) (PolarisKeyUpdate/Install.swift) streams through the client's transport (PolarisTransport.stream) into <to>.part, resumes with Range and If-Range on the payload SHA-256 (206 appends after re-hashing the part, 200 restarts, 416 verifies), maps a refusal to the body's registered wire code, and verifies size and SHA-256 before the file appears at <to>; the replayer runs all three steps of release-fetch-gated.json.

update.feeds.note: client.update.feedUrl(_:channel:velopackChannel:buildId:) over updateFeedURL (PolarisKeyUpdate/Install.swift); FeedUrlMatrixTests drives every feed-url-matrix.json row.

update.content.note: PolarisKeyCore's feedContent, holdsOf (stampHolds) and decideUpdate with UpdateContentInput (selectPackRows, the composition, prestage, contentBlock, packs; bootDecision gives required only for revoked required content); runUpdateCheck runs P4-13 §2.5 steps 10–14. ContentDecisionConformanceTests drives every feedContentCases and contentRows vector; UpdateClient.decide() builds the content input from update.packs.

update.driver.note: Sparkle on macOS: PolarisSparkle.start(client:channel:bundle:userDriver:) (PolarisKeyUpdate), and PolarisSparkleUserDriver (PolarisKeyUpdateUI, UK-08.6), the SwiftUI SPUUserDriver and its one update window; SparkleUserDriverTests and SparkleUserDriverMappingTests (the mapping table, every reply once, no invented percentage, nothing after an error).

update.bootguard.note: PolarisKeyCore AppBootGuard (client.bootGuard, client.markBootAttempt/confirmBoot with PolarisKeyUpdate): bootGuardAction over a launch counter kept beside the credential (Store record boot-guard); an Apple app has no previous build to roll back to, so after MAX_FAILED_BOOTS it journals P6-03 boot_rolled_back (code no-previous) once and answers rollBackUnavailable; the first confirmed launch of a new build journals update_confirmed. client.boot() marks the attempt and confirms BOOT_OK_SECONDS after ready.

outlet.detect.note: PolarisKeyCore detectOutlet over PolarisKeyUpdate readOutletSignals: AppDistributor.current behind #available(iOS 17.4) (web from 17.5) raced against the 2 s deadline, AltStore's ALTBundleIdentifier, embedded.mobileprovision, the macOS _MASReceipt and ProductionSandbox, the signing leaf (SecCodeCopySigningInformation) and the product's Caskroom link. UpdateClient detects at its first decision when the host names no outlet.

crash.tags.note: client.crashTags(deliverable:build:) and crashTagsFor(...): release <deliverable>@<version>[+<build>], environment the channel, pkey.outlet the outlet the update client resolved, left out while unknown, over the Worker's Sentry vectors (CrashTagsTests).

packs.record.note: PolarisKeyCore's verifyReleaseRecord with pin.kind (pack records fetched by the content stamp's pin) and PolarisKeyPacks' verifyMarker for embedded baselines; PackRecordConformanceTests drives every packRecordCases and markerCases vector.

packs.revoke.note: PolarisKeyCore's revocationOf, verifyRevocation and newerRevocation (every revocationCases vector); PackEngine keeps the sibling revocations.json (revocationsStored in state.json first, never created empty, re-verified per entry on load, relearn, the 256-target cap, torn and unreadable rules, recoverState clears relearn) and refuses revoked releases with pack-revoked (detail relearn for a refused baseline it cannot fetch).

packs.delegation.note: PolarisKeyCore verifyReleaseRecord (the delegated path, steps 13 and 16), verifyDelegation, recordRevoked and PolarisKeyPacks dataOnlyRefusal; the PackEngine fetches and caches delegations, refuses non-data-only delegated installs with pack-not-data-only, stores PackInstall.delegation and refuses releases under a revoked delegation (pack-revoked, detail delegation); DelegationConformanceTests drives every delegationCases and dataOnlyCases vector.

packs.plan.note: PolarisKeyPacks' plan, selectVariant and planTarget; every plan-matrix.json row, variant case and target case in PlanMatrixTests.

packs.index.files.note: PolarisKeyPacks' parseFilesIndex, checkPaths and treeDigest; filesIndexCases in ContentConformanceTests, read from the checkout.

packs.index.chunks.note: PolarisKeyPacks' parseChunkIndex and parseChunkIndexBytes (u64 from two little-endian u32 reads composed byte by byte, saturated at 2^53); chunkIndexCases in ContentConformanceTests under both libzstd paths.

packs.apply.full.note: applyFull, streamed through libzstd's ZSTD_decompressStream (and one-shot without it); applyCases under both paths.

packs.apply.file.note: applyFile with the type-neutral container rebuild; applyCases under both paths.

packs.apply.chunk.note: applyChunk (seed map, chunkRuns, repair pass, run journal resume) over chunkRangeFetch: one bounded Range per run with If-Range and Accept-Encoding identity through URLSession, an exact Content-Range and ETag, never multi-range. PackEngine keeps seed indexes under <packs root>/index/, seeds across packs and embedded baselines, and falls back on a refused range; the chunk applyCases in ContentConformanceTests and ChunkSyncTests.

packs.apply.delta.note: libzstd 1.5.7 (vendored C target, official source release): ZSTD_DCtx_refPrefix with ZSTD_d_windowLogMax; the window check runs in the applier before every prefix decode, macOS and iOS alike.

packs.delta.feed.note: feedContent reads the feed's deltas menu (both caps, both uniqueness rules, a non-payload entry dropped alone), withFeedDeltas merges it into the selected container variant before planTarget, and PackEngine tries at most one feed-offered delta per install (fallback on a failed fetch or any delta verdict), journalling it as feedDelta for resume; UpdateClient hands PacksClient the menu of the feed each check used (fresh or stale) and reads the committed feed from the cache when the engine starts.

packs.state.note: PackEngine over DirPackStorage in the platform data directory (excluded from backups): journal, resume with Range/If-Range, atomic pointer swap with F_FULLFSYNC, confirm, rollback, GC roots, embedded baselines, a torn state.json held aside, an unreadable one refusing every write; packSetId on devices/report.

packs.handlers.note: update.packs.registerHandler (PackHandler: supports, check over a newly staged payload before the state commit -> pack-type-check-failed, activate with the installed payload, deactivate); files.tree, data.json and l10n.table built in (hot: versioned directory plus pointer swap); ml.model registered by the host; custom.* through registerHandler, under the same path rules.

packs.type.godot.zip.note: P4-16: a godot.zip is mounted only by Godot's load_resource_pack.

packs.type.l10n.table.note: P4-16: L10nTableHandler (built in): PO, CSV and JSON tables by plain parsers (L10n.swift, scanned as Unicode scalars), BCP-47 locale matched to the variant; tables(packId), onActivate/onDeactivate.

packs.type.data.json.note: P4-16: DataJsonHandler (built in): every file strict JSON (strictParse), formatVersions listed by the host; documents(packId).

packs.type.audio.bank.note: P4-16: audio banks load through a game engine's middleware.

packs.type.ml.model.note: P4-16: MlModelHandler (host-registered): model.json runtime, quantisation and RAM/VRAM needs against the host budget, then the host load test before model(packId) swaps.

packs.transport.apple.note: SP-S08: PolarisKeyUpdate's AppleAssetPackTransport (a PackPlatformTransport over P5-05's AssetPackClient, set as PacksOptions.platformTransport): the level's asset pack <pack>-c<contentApi> (dots to hyphens), files under pkey/<asset pack>/ resolved with url(for:) on every call and never persisted, ensure with progress forwarded. The engine plans a carried pack only through the platform (plan-transport-unsupported while it is unavailable, never a CDN fallback), verifies the marker and the payload or treeDigest against the signed record, floats to a later unrevoked seq, and never commits the copy to the state. Unsupported version below iOS / macOS 26.4 and outlet without the Background Assets Info.plist keys. Stub-proven in PlatformTransportTests; the TestFlight device run is the owner's, as for Godot's P5-08.

packs.transport.steam.note: P5-08 covers Godot only; macOS Swift apps have no Steam-depot transport owner.

ui.stages.note: bootTransition and the stage-matrix replay (StageMatrixTests); client.boot() drives it end to end (discover, guard, sync, keyless reacquire under an open policy, gate, decide and fetch hooks installed by PolarisKeyUpdate, mount).

ui.boot.note: client.boot() (PolarisKey/Boot.swift): with no token under an open registration policy it registers keylessly before the sync pass; boot-cold-register.json replays through it.

ui.kit.note: UK-07: PolarisKeyUI on a pure-Swift presentation core (PolarisKeyUICore) for iOS and iPadOS 26 and macOS: PolarisKeyGate (one gate; `.polarisKey(client)` and `.polarisKeyGate(client)` both draw it; update banner, sheet and progress; toasts), sign-in, offline activation, boot stops (offline, blocked, declined, error, consent), account and licence, settings, devices and the update prompt, each laid out by the space it gets; the product leads (theme, the .polarisKeyPresentation seam, the bundle, a monogram); QR on TV only (D-67). Proof: PolarisKeyUICoreTests, the iPhone snapshot baselines with the accessibility audit, and KitRulesTests. BUILT UX review UXR-SWIFT plus one fix round (KX-SW-FIX).

ui.kit.manage.note: PX-W8: PolarisKeyGate shows Replace a device on device-limit (a button on macOS and iOS, a QR on tvOS).

ui.kit.account.note: I-10b.13: License in another account (a refusal with Sign in to that account when the server gave a valid signInUrl, a QR on tvOS), the gate model's D3 mapping (PolarisKeyGateModel.kitOutcome: chooseLicense is the matrix's choose) with LicenseChoiceModel wired into the gate (presentLicenseChoice, selectLicense, confirmLicenseChoice, openChoiceReplace, replaceChoiceDevice, cancelLicenseChoice), and the signed-in line "Signed in as {name} · {tier} license".

ui.kit.keyentry.note: I-10b.13: the key-entry-limit refusal (the matrix's key-entry-limit result) with Add {product} to your account opening the server's manageUrl (a QR on tvOS), shown only for a valid link; Use a different key stays beside it. The entries-left line after a successful activation is not drawn (copy exists; no matrix row yet).

ui.cli.portal.note: This SDK ships a widget kit (ui.kit) that shows only server or integrator links; the terminal kit's product page link is the headless SDKs' expectation (ui.cli.portal).

ui.cli.mount.note: This SDK ships a widget kit (ui.kit); the terminal drop-ins are the headless SDKs' expectation.

ui.cli.contract.note: This SDK ships a widget kit (ui.kit); the terminal kit's contract is the headless SDKs'.

ui.gate.note: PolarisKeyUICore runs the gate family of ui-matrix.json (UIMatrixTests); PolarisKeyUI's .polarisKeyGate draws PolarisKeyGate, Boot (the first paint), StatusScreen, GraceBanner and the toast, rendered on the iOS 26 simulator in both schemes with performAccessibilityAudit (examples/ui/swiftui KitRenderTests; baselines in Tests/PolarisKeyUISnapshotTests/__Snapshots__). iOS and iPadOS; the Mac pass is UK-08.

ui.activate.note: The activate family (UIMatrixTests; KeyVerdict is the Worker's key shape, so the Activate/parsed row's 20-character key is recorded as a corpus defect); Welcome and Activate rendered on the simulator, both schemes, AX3 and AX5, landscape, native and the iOS 18 material fallback. OfflineActivation is the core's only (off on iOS).

ui.signin.note: The signIn family (SignIn with its automatic steps and key refusal, SignInHandoff, LicenseChoice, NearbyApproval) in UIMatrixTests (ui-matrix v7); NearbyApprovalView over NearbyApprovalModel (states only; the nearby protocol is CC-15); the one sign-in form (SignInView) over the SDK's device-code primitives, every state rendered. The in-app license choice draws from I-04's views once the SDK carries the grant (I-10a).

ui.devicelimit.note: The deviceLimit family; DeviceLimitView (the browser mode on the key path, and the radio list when the inputs carry devices) rendered on the simulator.

ui.devices.note: The devices family; DevicesSection, a pane for the host's settings, rendered on the simulator.

ui.update.note: The update family; UpdatePromptView (the glass banner, the mandatory screen), UpdateProgressView and ReleaseNotesView rendered on the simulator; the Mac update window (UpdateWindowView, UK-08.6) is drawn by PolarisSparkleUserDriver.

ui.settings.note: The settings family; AccountAndLicenseSection and SettingsSection, panes in the host's font, rendered on the simulator. macOS (UK-08.4): PolarisKeySettingsPane, the Account tab for a Settings scene, and PolarisKeyCommands (Check for Updates…, Manage License…, Sign Out…), driven by KitSettingsMacTests in CI.

ui.paywall.note: The paywall family; PaywallView (the browser hand-off; StoreKit's store view is UK-25) and EntitlementGate rendered on the simulator.

ui.theme.note: The theme family (KitIdentity.theme); .polarisKeyTheme with the product accent through PolarisAccent, native, Drift Kart's light accent and the ink fallback rendered on the simulator; KitRulesTests.

ui.i18n.note: The i18n family against the ICU tables gen:brand writes for the core (Resources/kit-copy.json); de and ja renders of the main states on the simulator.

commerce.receipt.note: client.commerce (PolarisKey/CommerceClient.swift): binding() and claim(store:payload:) with claimAppStore/claimSteam/claimPlay, a forced sync after a granted claim, attest-and-retry on attestation_required; purchase(productID:) runs binding, StoreKit 2 purchase(appAccountToken: bindingId), claim, finish only after the claim, sync; restore() and the Transaction.updates loop claim and finish after the claim. Without StoreKit purchase/restore answer the typed runtime N/A.

sync.keyring.note: client.keyring (PolarisKey/SyncKeyring.swift, over PolarisKeyCore/Sync: CryptoKit HKDF, AES.GCM and HMAC, RFC 9180 mode_base written out over DeviceKeyPort.dh for open and an ephemeral Curve25519 key for seal): create(), unlock() (opens this device's wrap through the port's dh, so the agreement key never leaves the store), wrapTo()/removeWrap(), setRecoveryCode()/recover(), reset()/adopt()/openAdopted(), acceptRingChange(confirmed:), attach(_:) feeding setRoot, and the codec. The first root pins {ringId, epoch, rootKid} per product in the Core store; a served ring that differs is ringChanged and is never opened. The root is also kept in one Keychain item (sync-root, AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, never synchronizable) that is used only while it matches the pin; forget() drops the root and the pin and runs from the release hook (a Keychain delete that fails stops the sign-out). Every type holding key material prints as redacted. SyncVectorsTests (hkdf, envelope, blind, canonicalJson, hpkeAnchor, wrap, recovery and adopt cases, plus an HPKE.Sender cross-check), SyncKeyringTests and the keyring-* transcripts in TranscriptTests.

connect.identity.note: client.connect (ConnectClient): identity() registers the device keys on first need (PUT devices/keys with the keys proof; a memory-only key store is invalid-options unless ConnectOptions.allowEphemeralKeys), fetches GET connect/identity, verifies the roster and certificate (PeerDocs, from peerCertCases, ringCases, peerAdmissionCases) against the effective trust set, binds them to this device and its keys, refuses a stale, foreign or unlisted roster, and keeps the roster, the certificate and K_disc in one Keychain item (connect-state, this-device-only, never synchronized; K_disc prints as redacted). Every fetch replaces K_disc; the previous key is kept for 24 hours from first seen and dropped when a device was lost or re-keyed. A held identity with more than 3.5 days of certificate is served without a request unless refresh. An unreadable record is store-failed and never overwritten. leave() (called first on sign-out and release, which fail closed) deletes the record; with none held it touches nothing. listDevices() reads connect/devices. Typed: account_required, device_keys_required and ring_too_large come back verbatim; the service off is the product N/A. The connect transcripts replay with the relay slice.

connect.noise.note: PolarisKeyCore PeerNoise: Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 over CryptoKit, a zero DH refusing with dh_zero; PeerNoiseTests replays noise-vectors.json.

connect.protocol.note: PolarisKeyCore peer codecs, frames, relay envelopes, SAS and the peer session (modes a, v, p; commit-reveal SAS, handshake limiter), PeerLink, and the trust manager's accept-peer; PeerBytesTests, PeerCodecTests, PeerSessionTests, PeerSessionSASTests, ConnectSessionTests and TrustAcceptPeerTests replay peer-matrix.json.

connect.lan.note: PolarisKeyPlatform BonjourBrowse and BonjourPipes (Network.framework: NWBrowser, NWListener, NWConnection; dial policy G6 and D-10 before the first byte, accept gate and 30 s authentication bound) and PolarisKey ConnectLan (advert rotation, browse index, dial, wrong_peer, session caps); the Info.plist needs NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription and the NSBonjourServices entry _pkeypeer._tcp, and a sandboxed macOS app needs com.apple.security.network.client and .server; BonjourBrowseTests, BonjourPipesTests, ConnectLanTests.

connect.relay.note: client.connect.relayTicket() and PolarisKey ConnectRelay (URLSessionWebSocketTask with the pkey-relay.1 subprotocol and the ticket, reconnect policy, LIMIT and close codes 4001/4003/4008/4009, mode-a relay sessions, pacing, 8 MiB outbox cap with per-session accounting); ConnectRelayTests, ConnectRelaySessionTests, ConnectRelayTicketTests; TranscriptTests replays connect-relay-ticket and connect-relay-quota.

connect.app.note: client.cloudConnect (CloudConnect): start, stop, peers, devices, open and onChannel, LAN then relay, the G21 off switches, G9 and the sign-out order, a bounded stop with a forced abort (D-12); CloudConnectTests.
